title: Early blues singers and the mistaken 'Crazy Blues' record
summary: The talk turns to Bessie Smith, Ida Cox and Ma Rainey, and Price tells how the Crazy Blues record he bought turned out to be Bert Williams.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Blind Lemon Jefferson I think was almost the first of that kind of a singer which we now call a Country Blues...
Right, they hadn't done very much of that. 'Cause, well, during those days you had Bessie Smith, Ida Cox...

Yeah, Ma Rainey and Bert Williams. Incidentally.....let me tell you a story. One time my mother...Mamie Smith had made "The Crazy Blues." It was a very, very popular thing. So they said...wanted me to go and buy "The Crazy Blues." Now, instead of my going to the black store to buy it, I went to the white store to buy it. And I asked for "The Crazy Blues." The guy gave me

this "Crazy Blues" in a package and I went home and they said, "now if you break this I'm not going to exchange it." you know. So I walked very carefully and then I got home and they had a Gramophone, and my mother wound this thing up and put a needle in and put this "Crazy Blues" on and they thought that they were going to hear Mamie Smith and out came Bert Williams singing "The Crazy Blues." (Laughter)
